title: perf(desktop): compositor draws at the capture rate and pauses (audit REC-A7)
body:
Refs NIW2-401 · Closes audit finding **REC-A7** ([record lens A](https://github.com/niway-dev/kaipu-record/blob/main/apps/documentation/src/content/docs/audits/2026-10-15/findings/record-a.md)) · Spec: `apps/documentation/src/content/docs/specs/2026-10-28-niw2-401-compositor-cadence.md` (first commit of this branch) · Backlog note: `backlog/recording-compositor-perf.md`

> **Not measured in the app yet — please measure before merging.** The spec asks for the before/after draw rate and CPU on a ProMotion MacBook. This worker could not do it: the runner Mac mini has a 60 Hz 1080p display, and an Electron renderer started from the agent session never answers (`executeJavaScript("1+1")` times out, with or without Chromium's sandbox), so even a synthetic rVFC/rAF probe could not run. The code is safe if rVFC does stall (see R2 below), but the size of the win is unknown. Steps are in **How to test it yourself**.

## What changed and why

The compositor redrew the native frame (≈5.9 MP resample with `imageSmoothingQuality: "high"`) on every `requestAnimationFrame` — up to 120 Hz on ProMotion — while `captureStream(frameRate)` and mediabunny only use 30/s. It also kept drawing while the take was paused.

- **`recording-compositor.ts`**: draws are driven by `video.requestVideoFrameCallback` (one call per new source frame), or `requestAnimationFrame` when rVFC is missing. A draw sooner than `1000 / frameRate − 2` ms after the previous one is skipped. A 1 s heartbeat (250 ms tick) redraws a static screen. New `pause()` / `resume()`: pause cancels the callback and the heartbeat; resume draws once and follows the source again; both are idempotent and no-ops after `stop()`. `stop()` logs one line per take: `[recording-compositor] N draws, M source frames in Ts (X draws/s, cap 30) via requestVideoFrameCallback|requestAnimationFrame`.
- **`recorder-engine.ts`**: the take's `pause()` / `resume()` call `compositor?.pause()` / `compositor?.resume()` (resume redraws before the source samples again).
- **Docs**: cadence paragraph in `backlog/recording-compositor-perf.md`; plan `plans/audit-2026-10-15/25-compositor-cadence.md` deleted and its row removed from `00-index.md`. I left the index's "11 of 36 shipped" counter alone so the parallel batch-5 PRs don't all conflict on that line.

**One deviation from the spec's code.** The spec stamps `lastDrawAt = performance.now()` at the end of `draw()`. On a 60 Hz rAF clock with a 5 ms draw, the next frame at +33.3 ms is then only 28.3 ms after the stamp (< 31.3 ms), so it skips to every third frame: **21 draws/s instead of 30** (the test `keeps the capture rate on a 60 Hz clock even when a draw takes a few ms` fails with the spec's version — checked by mutating it). Here a frame-driven draw is stamped with the callback's frame time; heartbeat and resume draws use `performance.now()`. The Review Focus lines are unchanged.

**One small addition.** The spec arms the 500 ms rVFC→rAF guard once at start and skips it if the take is paused inside that window, which would leave such a take on heartbeat-only (1 fps) if rVFC never fires. The guard is armed in `start()` instead, so `resume()` re-arms it while no source frame has arrived yet.

## R1, R2 and the mediabunny re-check

- **mediabunny 1.61.4 (the installed version) re-checked:** `MediaStreamVideoTrackSource.pause()` only drops frames; it never touches the compositor, so the finding still holds. Also: with a `frameRate` option (the engine passes one), the source runs its own 250 Hz timer that **repeats the last frame** at `frameRate`, so the MP4 should stay constant-rate even when the canvas repaints less often.
- **R1 (VFR gaps on a static screen):** per the mediabunny code above, the encoded timeline should not have gaps; the 1 s heartbeat stays anyway, as specified. *Inferred from reading mediabunny, not confirmed with `ffprobe`* — step 4 below confirms it.
- **R2 (rVFC on a detached `<video>` in the hidden window):** not measured (see top). The guard switches to rAF if no rVFC callback has fired 500 ms after start, so a stalled rVFC degrades to "rAF capped at frameRate", not to a frozen recording. The stop log says which clock the take ended on.

## How I verified it

- New `recording-compositor.test.ts` (10 tests: first draw, per-frame draws, the 30/s cap with 60 Hz frames, pause/resume, idempotence and post-stop, stop, rAF fallback cap, the 60 Hz draw-cost case, the 500 ms rVFC→rAF switch and staying on rVFC once frames arrive, heartbeat). Run first against the old code: 8 of 10 failed.
- Two new tests in `recorder-engine.test.tsx` (engine pause/resume reach the compositor; no throw without one). The first failed before the engine change.
- `bun run verify` — twice in a row, both green. Note: this machine has no `node` on PATH, and under Bun's node shim 5 untouched tests fail for runtime reasons (Bun `BuildMessage: ModuleNotFound` for a `?worker_file` URL, `null` vs `undefined`); with Node 22 on PATH (`export PATH=$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v22.22.2/bin:$PATH`) everything passes.
- `bun run check-types` in `apps/kaipu-record`.

## How to test it yourself

On a ProMotion MacBook, non-16:9 built-in screen (so the compositor runs), 30 fps balanced; once without and once with a watermark. Build `main` and this branch in two worktrees.

1. Record 60 s of a looping video and 60 s of a static desktop; in one take, pause for 10 s halfway.
2. Renderer CPU: `top -pid <renderer pid> -l 12 -s 5`, averaged, before vs after (note the GPU process too). Expected: lower after, near zero during the pause.
3. Draws/s: this branch prints `[recording-compositor] … draws/s … via …` at stop (renderer console / terminal). Expected ≤ 30 and `via requestVideoFrameCallback`; if it says `requestAnimationFrame`, rVFC stalled in the hidden window (R2) and the cap still holds. `main` has no counter; its rate is the display refresh rate.
4. `ffprobe -v error -select_streams v -count_frames -show_entries stream=nb_read_frames,avg_frame_rate,duration file.mp4` before vs after, especially on the static take (R1: `nb_read_frames ≈ 30 × duration`). Scrub the file in the editor and export it.

If `main` turns out to draw at ≈30/s already, this change only buys the pause saving — worth noting on the ticket.

Run: agent-runner attempt 1, session 9fdd5ff1-7a89-419d-acbb-5aeae1ab1c60, Mac mini
